page: Amazon Web Services p6-b300.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The host system integrates 192 dedicated virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores powered by an x86_64 Intel processor operating at 2.4 GHz with two execution threads per core. System memory comprises 4,096 GB of system RAM, providing approximately 21.33 GB per physical core to support data preprocessing and host-side execution pipelines.

Hardware acceleration is driven by an array of 8 NVIDIA B300 GPUs equipped with a collective 2,149 GB of GPU VRAM. For persistent staging and high-speed data access, the platform includes 30,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Inter-node coordination and high-throughput communication are supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 6,400 Gbps, while zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Given the density of accelerator memory, host memory, and network throughput, this server type is engineered for distributed deep learning training, massive large language model inference pipelines, and matrix-intensive computational workloads. Qualitative cost efficiency reflects this top-tier hardware class; operational value requires saturating the 8-way GPU cluster, large local NVMe array, and multi-terabit network fabric to minimize idle overhead.
description: Amazon Web Services p6-b300.48xlarge is a high-density accelerated computing instance designed for distributed artificial intelligence and computational engineering. Hardware acceleration is provided by 8 NVIDIA B300 GPUs delivering 2,149 GB of combined VRAM. Local high-speed storage is integrated directly via 30,400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, complemented by a baseline network interface speed of 6,400 Gbps. These aggregated resources cater to ultra-scale deep learning model training, distributed inference, and large-scale parallel simulations. Resource efficiency relies on complete utilization of the massive GPU memory footprint, broad network pipes, and local NVMe storage, making it suited for intensive clustered workloads requiring maximum throughput and low data transfer latency across nodes.
